answer: An auditor would note that a farm lives or dies at its kernel of scheduling: honest work occupies scarce slots, clones try to stack them. So each lagoon-shaped market posts one kernel rule: every admitted identity binds a hardware root of trust to its payout address, and only one address may root to one device per fable-told epoch, verified by a challenger posing a fresh arithmetic fable. A clone farm needs thousands of distinct devices; recycling one device for many addresses forfeits every payout those addresses ever drew.
